Theorem
[Fundamental Theorem of Algebra]

↗ thm:fundamental-group-of-circle

1. ch1:1.8\group Fundamental Group

Every nonconstant polynomial over $\C $ has a complex root.

Proof

\sketch If $p(z)=z^n+a_1z^{n-1}+\cdots +a_n$ has no zero, normalize $p(re^{2\pi is})/p(r)$ to obtain loops in $S^1$. Varying $r$ makes them homotopic to the null loop at $r=0$. For $r>1+\sum |a_i|$, the homotopy $z^n+t(a_1z^{n-1}+\cdots +a_n)$ has no zero on $|z|=r$, so the same loop is homotopic to degree $n$. The circle theorem forces $n=0$, a contradiction.

□

The constructive proof by Sperner is cited in \cite{AignerZiegler1999}.
